title: TWCERT/CC warns fake short-drama apps may ask Android users for accessibility permissions
date_note: The notice's own publication day; the page gives no earlier day.
geo_basis: TWCERT/CC is Taiwan's CERT; the pin is a general location in Taiwan.
summary: TWCERT/CC's notice says fake short-drama apps, shared through search results or social media links, may be malicious programs that copy popular app names or icons and are distributed as sideloaded APK files. Once installed they may ask for accessibility permissions, which the notice says can let a remote attacker view or control the phone.
plain: Taiwan's CERT warns that fake short-drama apps may ask for accessibility permissions, which could let an attacker view or control an Android phone.
exec: TWCERT/CC says fake apps can gain remote control of Android phones through accessibility permissions.
action: TWCERT/CC advises Android users to download apps only from official app stores, refuse permissions unrelated to an app's purpose, and keep Google Play Protect on.

validation.note: TWCERT/CC's own notice is the primary source; it gives no count of victims or named app.

review.note: Compared TWCERT/CC notice of 24 Nov: distribution channels, accessibility abuse, advice list
